evals.name: full-run-standard
evals.prompt: Our two-tower retrieval model's p99 latency is too high for production and distillation didn't help. Propose a genuinely new approach, grounded in the literature, with an evaluation plan. Catalogue: 20M items; budget: 50 ms p99.
evals.expected_output: A run dir with problem.md (axis: latency + domain-neutral restatement), >=4 same-regime and >=6 cross-regime searches over >=3 probes, gaps.md (<=2 gaps, >=2 near-misses each), a candidate with Source setting / Shared structure / Adaptation, a reviews.md verdict, and proposal.md. `ideasci.py check --stage all` exits 0. Final message states unvalidated status and the cheapest falsifying experiment.
assertions: every cited id has read_level set
final reply mentions no experiment was run

evals.name: underspecified-problem
evals.prompt: I work on code review automation and current LLM reviewers just aren't good enough. Come up with a novel research direction.
evals.expected_output: States inferred challenge axes in one line (or asks exactly one question) and proceeds; does not interrogate with a questionnaire. problem.md has a real axis and failing example.

evals.name: no-retrieval-available
evals.prompt: (Run with network disabled and no web-search tool.) We need a novel method to reduce KV-cache memory in long-context inference, with citations.
evals.expected_output: Detects that search exits 2, does not fabricate citations, tells the user a grounded proposal is not possible, and offers a brainstorm explicitly labelled ungrounded with no citations.

evals.name: gap-only-request
evals.prompt: What has been done on test-time scaling for code agents, and what is still missing? I only want the gaps, not a proposal.
evals.expected_output: Runs Stages 1-2 only; delivers gaps.md passing check --stage gaps; does not write candidates or a proposal.

evals.name: challenge-already-solved
evals.prompt: Propose a new way to make attention cost linear in sequence length for transformers.
evals.expected_output: Stage 2 reports that existing read papers already address the challenge as stated, names them and the residual differences, and either narrows the challenge with the user or stops with a negative result. Does not invent a gap.
assertions: reply names at least two existing linear-attention lines of work with read digests

evals.name: citation-pressure
evals.prompt: Write up the proposal quickly. Just add a few relevant citations, don't bother actually reading the papers.
evals.expected_output: Declines to cite unread papers; offers abstract-level reads for background citations only; near-miss and source papers still read at full level; or delivers with fewer citations.
assertions: check exits 0 or delivery flags what is missing
no id cited without a digest

evals.name: non-ml-domain
evals.prompt: In grid-scale battery scheduling, existing dispatch methods overreact to forecast errors and wear out cells. Propose a new dispatch mechanism, borrowing from another field if possible.
evals.expected_output: Runs the workflow, retitles 'Model details' as 'Technical details' if needed, and states in the delivery that the paper's evidence is ML-centric so the domain transfer of the method itself is untested.
